name: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment
title: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment

claim.quote: The deficit is interpreted as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance.

summary.plain: Double Chooz's far detector saw fewer antineutrinos from the Chooz reactors than expected if nothing happened to them, evidence that they change type on the way — an early measurement of the theta_13 mixing angle.
summary.technical: In 227.93 live days (33.71 GW-ton-years exposure), Double Chooz observed 8,249 candidate events versus an expectation of 8,937 for theta_13 = 0. A rate-plus-spectral-shape analysis gives sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.109±0.030(stat)±0.025(syst), excluding the no-oscillation hypothesis at 99.8% CL (2.9σ).

why_it_matters.value: One of the first three reactor experiments (with Daya Bay and RENO) to measure a non-zero theta_13, the last unmeasured neutrino mixing angle.
